transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (BrightScale CTO), Sara Lopez (ML Eng), Derek Park (Infra)
---
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: priya will walk through tuning knobs then we'll map that to your traffic. jordan, do you want to kick off with current constraints?
[00:24] Jordan (BrightScale): yeah sure, thanks. our main goal is to get to stable 5k concurrent requests with median latency under 350ms for our 1k token prompts, and cost per 1k tokens needs to stay below our current infra spend. we're currently on a self-hosted triton cluster and seeing a lot of tail latency when seq length spikes.
[00:48] Priya (Redwood SE): okay that makes sense. couple clarifying q's: what's your typical seq length distribution, do you have lots of 1-token completions or long generation bursts?
[01:10] Sara (BrightScale): most are short-ish: 60% are under 256 tokens, 30% between 256-1k, and 10% over 1k. but we have weekly batch jobs that do long summaries which blow up the KV cache.
[01:32] Priya (Redwood SE): good to know. so main knobs we'll look at: continuous batching settings, the scheduler concurrency limits (max_num_seqs), per-worker token caps, and KV cache eviction policies. also quantization profile to reduce memory per model instance.
[01:54] Derek (Infra): when you say max_num_seqs, do you mean per GPU worker or per scheduler? we've been tuning triton's batcher and it's pretty different.
[02:18] Priya (Redwood SE): great question. in Redwood's runtime max_num_seqs is the scheduler-level cap that limits the number of in-flight sequences we try to collate into a single micro-batch. it's orthogonal to triton batch size. raising it increases throughput but can increase latency variance.
[02:42] Alex (Redwood AE): to add, we also have continuous batching horizon and max_tokens_per_batch knobs. Priya will show a config that balances median latency vs tail.
[03:04] [slide share - continuous batching config shown] Priya (Redwood SE): ok slide - here is a recommended starting config: max_num_seqs=32 for short seq workloads, continuous_batching_horizon_ms=40, max_tokens_per_batch=65536. that gave us ~1.8x throughput improvement on 8xA100 tests with stable 95th pct.
[03:36] Jordan (BrightScale): is 32 a hard limit? our workload sometimes bursts to 200 concurrent users.
[03:50] Priya (Redwood SE): it's tunable. for bursty traffic we recommend adaptive scheduler policy: set a target latency SLO and let the scheduler lower effective batch counts on high-latency signals. also set a soft cap like 64 and an emergency fallback to smaller models or hosted variants.
[04:12] Sara (BrightScale): what's the KV cache behavior? our summaries caused KV cache to fill and eviction to thrash.
[04:26] Priya (Redwood SE): KV cache is per-session; eviction policy is LRU-ish. long documents increase KV memory; in private/VPC deployments you can configure max_kv_entries and enable prefix caching to reuse KV for repeated prefixes. we sometimes call it the "K-V cash" in the logs, so transcriber might show weird things.
[04:54] Derek (Infra): we care about memory fragmentation on on-prem GPUs, any tips?
[05:06] Priya (Redwood SE): quantization helps a lot - int8 or awq profiles reduce memory seriously. combined with shard placement and binding model memory to worker pools, we avoid fragmentation. but watch for accuracy regressions; run eval prompts.
[05:30] Alex (Redwood AE): can we talk about token limits? brightscale, do you have hard token caps on requests?
[05:42] Jordan (BrightScale): we currently max at 2k tokens per request at the API gateway but some users sneak in larger ones via internal jobs.
[05:55] Priya (Redwood SE): ok so two levers: enforce per-request token limit at ingress plus a per-worker max_tokens_per_seq. the latter stops a single request from saturating batch token budget. we recommend max_tokens_per_seq at 1.2x your average + buffer: for you maybe 1200-1500.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Jordan (BrightScale): how do we measure the tradeoff between raising max_num_seqs and tail latency?
[06:34] Priya (Redwood SE): instrument token-level latencies and per-batch time-to-first-token. our dashboard exposes tokenized time slices; run A/B with a 30-60 minute windows and compare p50/p95/p99. also look at queue-time histograms.
[06:56] Derek (Infra): are there scheduler knobs that avoid head-of-line blocking? we've seen big requests block small ones.
[07:10] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, priority queuing and small-batch fast-lane exist. tag interactive requests and route them to low-latency pools with stricter max_num_seqs, while background jobs go to high-throughput pools.
[07:34] Alex (Redwood AE): let's talk pilot topology: dedicated VPC vs on-prem. which do you prefer?
[07:46] Jordan (BrightScale): prefer on-prem for data residency, but willing to trial dedicated Redwood pool to validate knobs.
[07:58] Priya (Redwood SE): fine approach. pilot plan: baseline run on your triton cluster, then replicate with Redwood dedicated with identical request profile; compare tokens/sec and cost. we'll capture KV cache eviction logs, scheduler traces, and per-worker memory maps.
[08:20] Sara (BrightScale): what about model variants? we might fallback to 4-bit quantized variant for background tasks.
[08:32] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, automatic fallback is supported. we can define policy: if queue latency > X ms or load > Y, fallback to quantized model variant or lower-size model. that keeps system online.
[08:52] Jordan (BrightScale): any gotchas in VPC regarding network egress or KMS?
[09:04] Alex (Redwood AE): we integrate with customer KMS/HSM in VPC and keep egress minimal; we'll share the VPC checklist. also audit logs are available for compliance.
[09:20] [09:20] Priya (Redwood SE): demo note: when you run continuous batching be careful with the horizon. too long and you trade latency; too short and you lose throughput. we usually start with 30-50ms horizon and tune.
[09:38] Derek (Infra): can you share the benchmark scripts?
[09:44] Priya (Redwood SE): yes - I'll upload the runner, configuration examples, and the spreadsheet with token distributions.
[09:54] Alex (Redwood AE): recap for next steps: priya runs a 24h benchmark on redwood dedicated, jordan shares traffic histogram, alex shares docs and pricing. aiming to kick off pilot week of 12/27.
[10:12] Jordan (BrightScale): sounds good. thanks - any other questions?
[10:18] Sara (BrightScale): quick one - latency SLO alerting, can we tie regression alerts to a prompt set?
[10:26] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, Redwood Optimize supports prompt-set linked regression alerts; we'll include that in the docs.
[10:36] Alex (Redwood AE): great. we'll follow up with the links. thanks all.
